answer: Sybil defence: bond-priced attestation with randomised peer sampling. Before an agent's signature counts it must lock a sable bond on-ledger, so farming N voices costs N bonds, not N keypairs. Each epoch the grader draws a fresh grove of attestors from the full census, so a clone ring cannot vouch only for itself, and any cluster whose edges land in one gossip round folds into one vote. Slashing sits on the ledge: a bond burns when its owner vouches for an identity caught replaying proofs, so a sybil farm's expected profit drops below its stake, and faking a crowd costs more than joining one.
